title: Going to bed before the visitor's footsteps cancels the visit with no penalty
where: src/game/home/knock.ts:252 (atDoor excludes phase 'wait'), knock.ts:291-296 (abandon() in 'wait' is silent), src/game/home/evening.ts:424-428 (bed blocked only when atDoor())
fix: Close the loophole in one of two ways, both reached from abandon(). (a) Block the bed while a visit is planned, not only at the door: in evening.ts:426 check `visit && visit.state.phase !== 'done'` (or add a 'planned' predicate to Visit). (b) Keep the bed open and resolve an early-bed skip as the visit arriving: in knock.ts:291-296, if st.phase === 'wait', call io.resolve(resultOf(st.kind, false)) before leaver()/go('done'), so it applies the fail (Heat +1 and the kind's toll and penalty). Option (b) also covers the auto-sleep path because startSleep() calls endVisit(). Add a test that sleeping in 'wait' cannot leave Heat or the toll unchanged.

title: A reload between the verdict and the next flush re-resolves a passed visit as a fail
where: src/game/home/knock.ts:196-200 (finish: resolve before go('leave')), knock.ts:298-300 (resume forces fail on phase 'act'), src/game/home/evening.ts:276-284 (applyResult -> homeFlags), src/game/run.ts:1645-1649 (homeFlags only calls persistSoon)
fix: In knock.ts finish(): set st.pass = pass and go('leave') BEFORE io.resolve(resultOf(...)), so any synchronous save inside applyResult (the Picker's loseCharm persist, run.ts:1392) records 'leave'. In evening.ts applyResult, replace run.homeFlags({}) with a synchronous save (a boundary persist, not persistSoon) so the outcome is written at the verdict. In resume() (knock.ts:298-300), do not re-resolve a visit in 'act' without a stored outcome: record the outcome in the snapshot first, or treat a restored 'act' as already resolved once st.pass is set. Test: restore with phase 'leave' (must not re-resolve) and with phase 'act' (fail), and a Picker steal followed by restore (no second toll or charm loss). Separately, fix run.flush/pagehide ordering so the run's pending write is flushed after save.update (or call app.save.flush() after run.flush()), or the post-verdict state is still lost on a normal reload.
